findings.explanation:
The tool compared 37 months in which your portfolio was worth at least NZ$500.
Each month, the smaller of what you bought and what you sold was about 18% of your portfolio on average. Over a year that adds up to about 217%.
Money you add and then buy shares with is not counted, because it is not sold.
A large study of US households called more than 8.8% a month frequent trading.
This is based on 71 of your own buy and sell decisions.
Your figure is more than 8.8% a month, so this pattern was found.

findings.explanation:
This is based on 37 times you sold a share.
On those days, you sold 55% of the winning positions you held and 1.8% of the losing positions you held.
The gap in favour of selling winners is bigger than luck would explain, so this pattern was found.

findings.title: Buying after a sharp rise
findings.threshold: Share of buys after a top-10% rise above 10%, with p below 0.05

evidence.note: Bought ASX:DEMOE on 2023-03-22, after it rose 28.4% in the 20 trading days before
Bought ASX:DEMOB on 2023-01-25, after it rose 24.1% in the 20 trading days before
Bought ASX:DEMOE on 2022-03-07, after it rose 16.6% in the 20 trading days before
Bought ASX:DEMOC on 2023-03-20, after it rose 10.3% in the 20 trading days before

findings.explanation:
This is based on 39 of your buys that had a full year of earlier prices.
4 of them (10%) came right after a big rise in the share's price.
A big rise means one in the top 10% of that share's rises over the year before.
By luck alone, about 10% of buys would come after a big rise.
Your share is not more than luck would explain, so this pattern was not found.
